set.body:
Supporting track of docs/plan.md.

Done when
A persistent instance runs on a host inside the institute network, reachable over https, with named accounts, a nightly backup and one restore drill that has been carried out and written down.

Design decisions
- Start on a host we control. A lab server is enough. An institutional machine and single sign-on are what the pitch asks for, so they cannot be preconditions of the MVP.
- Sign-in goes through the bundled Keycloak with named pilot accounts. Federating it to the institute directory, and qualifying the campus provider (F04.4), come with the pilot.
- Backups use the existing database and blob-store scripts. A plain restore brings back access that was revoked after the backup. RUN3 decides between enrolling the existing policy witness, which was built to prevent that, and keeping a restored instance closed until stewards have re-checked access. Further recovery qualification (EP4) stays parked.
- The demo instance (scripts/demo-instance.py) stays as it is for development and for the seeded rehearsals.

Order
RUN0 and RUN1 are the owner's. RUN2 can be built on any Linux machine now and moved to the pilot host when RUN1 lands. RUN3 follows RUN2. RUN4 starts this Friday on the seeded instance.
set.title: RUN: A real instance that people sign in to
